# Bank of England RSS Taxonomy (Experiments in Agents and Data Science)

> An unofficial, agent-maintained index of everything published through the Bank of England's public RSS feeds (news, speeches, publications, statistics, PRA publications, events, explainers and Bank Insights), organised into a subject taxonomy and refreshed weekly. 378 items; last updated 2026-11-16. Not affiliated with the Bank of England; all content and links belong to the Bank.

Each entry links to the original page on bankofengland.co.uk. Themes are assigned by transparent keyword rules (see scripts/taxonomy.py). Machine-readable data: data/items.json and data/items.csv.

## Dataset

- [items.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anorthernman-developer/experiments-in-agents-and-data-science/main/data/items.json): every archived item with theme, content type, dates and link
- [items.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anorthernman-developer/experiments-in-agents-and-data-science/main/data/items.csv): the same data as CSV
- [Latest weekly digest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anorthernman-developer/experiments-in-agents-and-data-science/main/weekly/latest.md): what is new this week, grouped by theme
- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anorthernman-developer/experiments-in-agents-and-data-science/main/llms-full.txt): every item with its description in one file

## Source feeds

- [Bank Insights](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/bank-insights): Short analytical pieces from Bank staff.
- [Events](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/events): Conferences, workshops and Citizens' Panels hosted or attended by the Bank.
- [Explainers](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/knowledgebank): Plain-English explainers on economics and the Bank.
- [News](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/news): Press releases, letters, minutes and announcements.
- [Prudential regulation publications](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/prudential-regulation-publications): PRA consultation papers, policy statements, discussion papers and digests.
- [Publications](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/publications): Reports, papers, surveys, working papers and weekly reports.
- [Speeches](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/speeches): Speeches and panels by Bank of England policymakers and staff.
- [Statistics](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/rss/statistics): Statistical releases such as Money and Credit and effective interest rates.

The Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee and European hedgehog will represent UK wildlife and feature as the central images on our next series of...

Report on the Bank of England’s work under the Scottish and Northern Ireland Banknote Regulations 2009.
- [The promise to pay: what backs banknotes?](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/bank-insights/2026/the-promise-to-pay-what-backs-banknotes): 17 Sep 2026, Bank Insights. The Bank of England’s new strategy for backing our banknotes
- [How much is a banknote worth?](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/how-much-is-a-banknote-worth): 27 Sep 2018, Explainers (Knowledge Bank). While rare serial numbers often generate interest, banknotes will only ever be worth their face value to us.
- [How do we know how much money to print?](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/how-do-we-know-how-much-money-to-print): 19 Dec 2017, Explainers (Knowledge Bank). We mostly print money to replace old, worn-out banknotes. But it’s also up to demand.
- [Why are new banknotes made of polymer?](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/why-are-new-banknotes-made-of-polymer): 22 Nov 2017, Explainers (Knowledge Bank). Our new banknotes are made of polymer because it is cleaner, safer and stronger than paper.

Witnesses: Dave Ramsden, Nathan Monk and Victoria Cleland
- [Who pays for the Bank of England?](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/who-pays-for-the-bank-of-england): 30 Oct 2019, Explainers (Knowledge Bank). Although we’re a public body, each year we give around £350 million back to the public through HM Treasury.
- [The Bank of England in literature](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/the-bank-of-england-in-literature): 17 Nov 2017, Explainers (Knowledge Bank). We make an appearance in literature as a setting, an institution and even a character in itself.
